import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1057

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1057](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1057)
- [AGP94] Alford, W. R. and Granville, Andrew and Pomerance, Carl, There are infinitely many
  Carmichael numbers. Ann. of Math. (2) (1994), 703--722.
- [Er56c] Erdős, P., On pseudoprimes and Carmichael numbers. Publ. Math. Debrecen (1956),
  201--206.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
- [Ha08] Harman, Glyn, Watt's mean value theorem and Carmichael numbers. Int. J. Number Theory
  (2008), 241--248.
- [Li22] J. D. Lichtman, Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli and shifted primes
  without large prime factors. arXiv:2211.09641 (2022).
- [Po89] Pomerance, Carl, Two methods in elementary analytic number theory. (1989), 135--161.
-/

open Nat Real Filter Set
open scoped Topology Asymptotics

namespace Erdos1057


/--
Let $C(x)$ count the number of Carmichael numbers in the interval $[1,x]$.
-/
noncomputable def carmichaelCounting (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ({n : ℕ | IsCarmichael n ∧ (n : ℝ) ≤ x}.ncard : ℝ)

/--
Is it true that $C(x)=x^{1-o(1)}$?

This is discussed in problem A13 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun x ↦ Real.log (carmichaelCounting x) / Real.log x) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er56c] proved $C(x) < x \exp\left(-c \frac{\log x\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}\right)$
for some constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.upper_bound :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ x in atTop,
      carmichaelCounting x < x * Real.exp (-c * (Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x))) /
        Real.log (Real.log x)) := by
  sorry

/--
Pomerance [Po89] gave a heuristic suggesting that this is the true order of growth, and in fact
$C(x)= x \exp\left(-(1+o(1))\frac{\log x\log\log\log x}{\log\log x}\right)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.pomerance :
    answer(sorry) ↔ Tendsto (fun x ↦
      -(Real.log (carmichaelCounting x / x) * Real.log (Real.log x)) /
      (Real.log x * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log x)))) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Alford, Granville, and Pomerance [AGP94] proved that $C(x)\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.agp_infinite :
    Tendsto carmichaelCounting atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Alford, Granville, and Pomerance [AGP94] proved that $C(x)>x^{2/7}$ for large $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.agp_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (2 / 7 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
The lower bound $C(x)> x^{0.33336704}$ was proved by Harman [Ha08].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.harman_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (0.33336704 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
This exponent was improved to $0.3389$ by Lichtman [Li22].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_1057.variants.lichtman_lower_bound :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, carmichaelCounting x > x ^ (0.3389 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1057

reformulations.difference: The counting set ranges over ℕ without explicitly imposing either 1 ≤ n or compositeness outside IsCarmichael.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Specializing IsCarmichael n to base 1 forces Nat.FermatPsp n 1, which includes 1 < n and ¬n.Prime. Thus 0, 1 and primes are excluded, and adding the lower endpoint 1 ≤ n leaves the set unchanged. For positive bases, Nat.probablePrime_iff_modEq identifies the divisibility condition with the usual Fermat congruence. These equivalences and finiteness of the counting set for every real x were proved in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source's C(x)=x^{1-o(1)} is expressed as log(C(x))/log(x) tending to 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Eventually C(x)>0, while C(x)≤x for x≥0. Consequently the logarithmic limit is equivalent to Erdős's original formulation: for every ε>0, eventually C(x)>x^{1-ε}. It is also equivalent to an eventual identity C(x)=x^{1-ε(x)} with ε(x)→0, taking ε(x)=1−log(C(x))/log(x). Both equivalences were proved in Lean; small-input logarithm defaults do not affect them.

reformulations.difference: The exponential asymptotic formula is replaced by a limit of a normalized logarithm.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write A(x)=log(x)logloglog(x)/loglog(x). On a sufficiently large tail, all relevant arguments are positive and denominators nonzero. The Lean expression is exactly q(x)=−log(C(x)/x)/A(x). Thus q(x)→1 is equivalent to C(x)=x exp(−(1+ε(x))A(x)), with ε(x)=q(x)−1→0. This equivalence was proved in Lean. In Pomerance's paper, the heuristic lower bound together with Theorem 5.1's upper bound gives this exponential asymptotic.

reformulations.difference: Infinitude of Carmichael numbers is stated as the real-valued counting function tending to +∞.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An infinite set of Carmichael numbers contains finite subsets of every prescribed size; every sufficiently large cutoff contains each such subset. Conversely, if there were only finitely many Carmichael numbers, every cutoff count would be bounded by their total cardinality. The exact equivalence with Tendsto carmichaelCounting atTop atTop was proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: Lichtman's Corollary 1.2 says 'at least x^{0.3389}', whereas Lean uses a strict eventual lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These statements are equivalent for this counting function over real cutoffs. For every sufficiently large x, choose y>x before the next integer, so C(y)=C(x). An eventual non-strict bound then yields C(x)=C(y)≥y^{0.3389}>x^{0.3389}. The converse is immediate. The scratch file proves this equivalence for every positive real exponent.

review.notes: All eight declarations were checked; no mathematical discrepancies were found. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles with zero errors, and the equivalence lemmas have no sorryAx dependencies. Boundary checks establish finite counting sets, exclusion of 0/1/primes, eventual positivity, C(x)≤x, and counts C(560)=0, C(561)=1, C(1105)=2, C(1729)=3. Access limitations: https://www.erdosproblems.com/1057 consistently returned a Cloudflare challenge despite descriptive User-Agent headers, so its latest remarks and recorded status could not be checked directly. No status mismatch was evidenced by the accessible sources. Harman's full text was unavailable; its exact exponent was corroborated by Wikipedia and Lichtman's discussion, with the published abstract also consulted. Guy's A13 was available only through contents/search excerpts; the main conjecture was verified directly against Erdős's original paper. The reviewed file was not modified.
